changes.text: A reviewer classifies topics, scopes, sources, conflicts, and confidence. An isolated Codex CLI is preferred; when it cannot run, the current Session of any supported Agent host may review the same explicitly delimited untrusted-source bundle and submit schema-valid output. Reviewer output remains untrusted structured input and never receives canonical write authority.

changes.text: Reviewer selection order is the same for every supported Agent host: isolated Codex CLI, then the current host Session, then an explicitly configured fallback reviewer. A broken WindowsApps Codex executable must not silently cause a cross-vendor fallback while the current Session is capable of reviewing.

A broken WindowsApps Codex executable must not silently cause a cross-vendor fallback while the current Codex Session is capable of reviewing.

changes.text: `--host-session` names the Agent host that is running the command and accepts every supported host id, currently `codex` and `claude`. It must never be interpreted as a Codex-only switch, and a valueless `--host-session` is a usage error rather than a silent no-op.

A declared host session is what authorizes the current-Session reviewer fallback. Any declared host may complete the review handoff through `mdg adopt session-review`; only an undeclared host session leaves the run without that fallback.

`--yes` is an explicit, documented confirmation flag for `mdg init`. It restates the zero-touch default, and combining it with `--preview` or `--setup-only` is a usage error rather than a silently ignored contradiction.

Generated bootstrap instructions must name the host they are written for. A host entrypoint or global bootstrap must cite that host's own `--host-session` value and its own managed launcher directory, never another host's.
